19587-the-christmas-kalends-of-provence-.creator: Unknown
19587-the-christmas-kalends-of-provence-.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Fancy a mistral cutting keen  Across the sunlit wintry fields,  Fancy brown vines, and olives green,  And blustered, swaying, cypress shields. Fancy a widely opened door,  Fancy an eager outstretched hand,  Fancy--nor need you ask for more--  A heart-sped welcome to our land. Fancy the peal of Christmas chimes,  Fancy that some long-buried year  Is born again of ancient times--  And in Provence take Christmas cheer! In my own case, this journey and this welcome were not fancies but realities.

4061-the-fifteen-decisive-battles-of-the.title: The Fifteen Decisive Battles Of The World From Marathon To W
4061-the-fifteen-decisive-battles-of-the.creator: Sir Edward Creasy, M.A.
4061-the-fifteen-decisive-battles-of-the.description: A book by Sir Edward Creasy, M.A.. or his favourite topic, merely because they were battles, merely because so many myriads of troops were arrayed in them, and so many hundreds or thousands of human beings stabbed, hewed, or shot each other to death during them, would argue strange weakness or depravity of mind. Yet it cannot be denied that a fearful and wonderful interest is attached to these scenes of carnage.

5142-graustark.title: Graustark
5142-graustark.creator: George Barr McCutcheon
5142-graustark.description: A book by George Barr McCutcheon. When the idea of Mexico did occur to him he gave orders to pack his things, purchased interminable green tickets, dined unusually well at his club, and was off in no time to the unknown West.

arxiv-2212-06105.title: Magnon-Plasmon Hybridization Mediated by Spin-Orbit Interaction in Magnetic Materials
arxiv-2212-06105.creator: Anna Dyrdał 1, Alireza Qaiumzadeh 2, Arne Brataas 2, Józef Barnaś 1,3
arxiv-2212-06105.description: Abstract We propose a mechanism for magnon-plasmon coupling and hybridization in ferromagnetic (FM) and antiferromagnetic (AFM) systems. The electric field associated with plasmon oscillations creates a non-equilibrium spin density via the inverse spin galvanic effect. This plasmon-induced spin density couples to magnons by an exchange interaction.

arxiv-2302-07768.title: Combinatorial Depth Measures for Hyperplane Arrangements
arxiv-2302-07768.creator: Patrick Schnider, Pablo Soberón
arxiv-2302-07768.description: Abstract Regression depth, introduced by Rousseeuw and Hubert in 1999, is a notion that measures how good of a regression hyperplane a given query hyperplane is with respect to a set of data points. Under projective duality, this can be interpreted as a depth measure for query points with respect to an arrangement of data hyperplanes.

arxiv-2401-06842.title: Two rest-frame wavelength measurements of galaxy sizes at z < 1 z<1 : the evolutionary effects of emerging bulges and quenched newcomers 2024 Two rest-frame wavelength measurements of galaxy sizes at z < 1 z<1 : the evolutionary effects of emerging bulges and quenched newcomers – D
arxiv-2401-06842.creator: Angelo George, Ivana Damjanov, Marcin Sawicki, Stéphane Arnouts, Guillaume Desprez, Stephen Gwyn, Vincent Picouet, Simon Birrer, John Silverman
arxiv-2401-06842.description: Abstract We analyze the size evolution of 16000 16000 star-forming galaxies (SFGs) and 5000 5000 quiescent galaxies (QGs) with mass M ∗ > 10 9.5 M_{*}>10^{9.5} M ⊙ at 0.1 < z < 0.9 0.1<z<0.9 from the COSMOS field using deep CLAUDS+HSC imaging in two rest-frame wavelengths, 3000 3000 Å (UV light) and 5000 5000 Å (visible light).

arxiv-2409-17031.title: Null geodesics around a black hole with weakly coupled global monopole charge
arxiv-2409-17031.creator: Mohsen Fathi, J.R. Villanueva, Thiago R.P. Caramês, Alejandro Morales-Díaz
arxiv-2409-17031.description: Abstract In this paper, we study an asymptotically flat black hole spacetime with weakly nonminimally coupled monopole charge. We analytically and numerically investigate light ray propagation around such a black hole by employing the common Lagrangian formalism. Our analysis encompasses both radial and angular geodesics, for which we present analytical solutions in terms of incomplete Lauricella hypergeometric functions.

arxiv-2412-00967.title: Linear Probe Penalties Reduce LLM Sycophancy
arxiv-2412-00967.creator: Henry Papadatos, Rachel Freedman
arxiv-2412-00967.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are often sycophantic, prioritizing agreement with their users over accurate or objective statements. This problematic behavior becomes more pronounced during reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), an LLM fine-tuning stage intended to align model outputs with human values. Instead of increasing accuracy and reliability, the reward model learned from RLHF often rewards sycophancy.

arxiv-2505-23666.title: LoLA: Low-Rank Linear Attention with Sparse Caching
arxiv-2505-23666.creator: Luke McDermott lmcdermo@ucsd.edu, Robert W. Heath Jr. rwheathjr@ucsd.edu, Rahul Parhi rahul@ucsd.edu
arxiv-2505-23666.description: Abstract The per-token cost of transformer inference scales with context length, preventing its application to lifelong in-context learning. Linear attention is an efficient alternative that maintains a constant memory footprint, even on infinite context lengths. While this is a potential candidate for lifelong learning, it falls short in memory capacity.

arxiv-2506-03533.title: Go-Browse: Training Web Agents with Structured Exploration
arxiv-2506-03533.creator: Apurva Gandhi, Graham Neubig
arxiv-2506-03533.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Apurva Gandhi, Graham Neubig. One of the fundamental problems in digital agents is their lack of understanding of their environment. For instance, a web browsing agent may get lost in unfamiliar websites, uncertain what pages must be visited to achieve its goals. To address this, we propose Go-Browse, a method for automatically collecting diverse and realistic web agent data at scale through structured exploration of web environments.

arxiv-2507-02896.title: Dissecting Circles to Prove a Square: A Novel Geometric Proof of the Pythagorean Theorem Using Circular Segments and Area Decomposition
arxiv-2507-02896.creator: Luca Nathanael Chang
arxiv-2507-02896.description: Abstract The Pythagorean Theorem has been proved in hundreds of ways, yet it inspires fresh insights through geometry and trigonometry. In this paper, we offer a new proof based on three circles that circumscribe the sides of a right triangle.

pmc-10768550.title: Pulmonary involvement in primary Sjögren's syndrome: contribution of the different means in the systematic investigation
pmc-10768550.creator: Maysam Jridi, Yosra Cherif, Samar Derbal, Fatma Ben Dahmen, Meya Abdallah
pmc-10768550.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The prevalence of pulmonary involvement in primary Sjögren´s syndrome (pSS) varies depending on investigation methods. Our study aimed to identify the contribution of the different means of investigation in the systematic screening for pulmonary involvement in pSS. This is a retrospective and descriptive study including medical records of pSS patients, who validated the 2016 American College of Rheumatology/European League Against Rheumatism classification criteria for pSS and who had undergone pulmonary assessment. We enrolled 30 patients: twenty-nine females (97%) and one male (3%).

pmc-11457475.title: Clinicians’ roles and necessary levels of understanding in the use of artificial intelligence: A qualitative interview study with German medical students
pmc-11457475.creator: F Funer, S Tinnemeyer, W Liedtke, S Salloch
pmc-11457475.description: BackgroundArtificial intelligence-driven Clinical Decision Support Systems (AI-CDSS) are being increasingly introduced into various domains of health care for diagnostic, prognostic, therapeutic and other purposes. A significant part of the discourse on ethically appropriate conditions relate to the levels of understanding and explicability needed for ensuring responsible clinical decision-making when using AI-CDSS.

pmc-11641535.title: Various Forms of Cardiac Rehabilitation and Their Effect on Frailty Syndrome in Cardiac Patients—A Systematic Review
pmc-11641535.creator: Magdalena Wójciak, Natalia Świątoniowska-Lonc, Kinga Węgrzynowska-Teodorczyk
pmc-11641535.description: Background: The growing population of the elderly is accompanied by an increase in the number of people with frailty syndrome. Apart from advanced age, the occurrence of cardiovascular diseases is also one of the agents favorable to frailty that is a factor aggravating the disease prognosis. However, it is worth noting that this is an agent changeable by, i.a.

pmc-11867667.title: Validation of the adult asthma epidemiological score: a secondary analysis of the EPI-ASTHMA population-based study
pmc-11867667.creator: Catarina Laranjeira, Cristina Jácome, Rita Amaral, Filipa Bernardo, Jaime Correia-de-Sousa, Joao A Fonseca
pmc-11867667.description: AbstractObjectiveThe A2 score is an eight-question patient-reported outcome measure that has been validated for ruling in (score ≥4) and ruling out (score 0–1) asthma. However, this screening tool has been validated in a cohort similar to the derivation cohort used.

pmc-11969037.title: Knowledge attributes of public health management information systems used in health emergencies: a scoping review
pmc-11969037.creator: Barbara Burmen, Elliot Brennan, Maryam Mohammed Samaila, Allan Bell, Candice Vente, Landry Ndriko Mayigane
pmc-11969037.description: IntroductionLearning from public health emergencies has not always been possible due to suboptimal knowledge accrual from previous outbreaks. This study described the knowledge attributes of Health Management Information Systems (HMIS) that are currently used during health emergencies. It aims to inform the development of a “nuggets of knowledge” (NoK) platform to support agile decision-making and knowledge continuity following health emergencies.

pmc-12612679.title: One transcript, two functions: the emerging roles of dual-function RNAs
pmc-12612679.creator: Liz Maria Luke, Kai Papenfort, Cynthia Sharma
pmc-12612679.description: Bacteria use small regulatory RNAs (sRNAs) and small proteins to change gene expression and modulate cellular processes in response to changing environmental conditions. In addition, several transcripts have been reported to combine base-pairing sRNA activities and coding capacity. These transcripts are known as dual-function RNAs.

pmc-12656411.title: Cellular and Molecular Mechanisms of Micro- and Nanoplastics Driving Adverse Human Health Effects
pmc-12656411.creator: Antonio F Hernández, Marina Lacasaña, Aristidis M Tsatsakis, Anca Oana Docea, Yi Cao
pmc-12656411.description: Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) are increasingly recognized as emerging contaminants of concern for human health. Their small size, diverse composition, and reactive surface enable interactions with biological barriers and cellular systems. This comprehensive narrative review synthesizes and critically evaluates current evidence on the mechanistic effects of MNPs in humans and experimental models.

pmc-13390279.title: Predicting general practice trainee summative fellowship exam performance using commencement-of-training formative assessments: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-13390279.creator: Alison Fielding, Irena Patsan, Elizabeth Holliday, Jason Dizon, Jean Ball, Amanda Tapley, Ashley Blowes, Alexandria Turner, Linda Klein, Graham Lee, Parker Magin
pmc-13390279.description: BackgroundFellowship examinations in Australian vocational general practice training assess competency for unsupervised practice. Early identification of trainees at risk of failing these summative examinations facilitates pro-active remediation. This study aimed to explore the utility of formative pre-general practice assessments (PGAs), undertaken at the commencement of training, for predicting final summative examination performance.MethodsThis was a retrospective cohort study.

pmc-13574543.title: Exploratory single‐nucleus multiomics analysis of myeloid cell states associated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy response in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
pmc-13574543.creator: Mercy Ojetunde, Li Ma, Hillary G Goodney, Alyson M Stevens, Alan Mizener, Emidio E Pistilli, Sascha Ott, Kawther Abdilleh, Barbara Szomolay, Gangqing Hu, Timothy D Eubank, Brian A Boone
pmc-13574543.description: BackgroundPancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) continues to be one of the most lethal human malignancies, with the vast majority of patients ineligible for immunotherapy. Tumour‐associated macrophages (TAMs) are key regulators of the PDAC tumour microenvironment (TME), yet their transcriptional and epigenomic heterogeneity in the context of chemotherapy response is poorly understood.

pmc-13601740.title: Guiding the Application of Immunotherapy in Nonsmall Cell Lung Cancer: The Role of Biomarkers
pmc-13601740.creator: Yuting Sun, Xuelei Chu, Xinmiao Wang, Weina Li, Xiaoyu Zhu, Guanghui Zhu, Xinyi Ma, Xue He, Jie Li
pmc-13601740.description: Although immunotherapy has completely transformed the treatment landscape of nonsmall cell lung cancer (NSCLC), its wide application is still limited by the heterogeneity of patient responses, primary and acquired resistance, as well as the management challenges of immune‐related adverse events (irAEs).

pmc-13657527.title: Risk factors for post-PCI restenosis in patients with coronary heart disease and the development and validation of a nomogram prediction model
pmc-13657527.creator: Xin Jin, Zhengliang Dong, Dongsheng Chai
pmc-13657527.description: This study aimed to analyze risk factors for in-stent restenosis (ISR) following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with coronary heart disease and develop and validate a nomogram prediction model. Clinical data were retrospectively collected from 1135 patients with coronary heart disease who underwent PCI at our hospital between January 2015 and December 2024.

uslaw-usc-t20-s5506.title: 20 U.S.C. § 5506 — Environmental internships and fellowships
uslaw-usc-t20-s5506.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t20-s5506.description: United States Code, Title 20 (Education); Chapter 65 (National Environmental Education). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Postsecondary students and in-service teachers The Administrator shall, in consultation with the Office of Personnel Management and other appropriate Federal agencies, provide for internships by postsecondary level students and fellowships for in-service teachers with agencies of the Federal Government. (b) Purpose The purpose of internships.

uslaw-usc-t22-s7115.title: 22 U.S.C. § 7115 — Ensuring protection and confidentiality for survivors of human trafficking
uslaw-usc-t22-s7115.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t22-s7115.description: United States Code, Title 22 (Foreign Relations And Intercourse); Chapter 78 (Trafficking Victims Protection). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Definitions In this section— (1) the term “covered grant” means a grant from the Attorney General or the Secretary of Health and Human Services under section 7104(b), 7105(b), or 7105(f) of this title; and (2) the term “covered recipient” means a grantee.
